description: CloudSim is a framework for modelling and simulating cloud computing infrastructures and services. It represents data centres, physical hosts, virtual machines, containers, provisioning and allocation policies, energy-aware resources, data-centre network topologies and federated clouds, and it lets users stop, resume and insert simulation elements dynamically. It is developed by the Cloud Computing and Distributed Systems (CLOUDS) Laboratory at the University of Melbourne under Rajkumar Buyya; the current generation, CloudSim 7G, is described in Software: Practice and Experience (2025), and the repository was last updated in January 2026. Coverage: user-defined virtual data centres of any size, with no real geographic data; resolution is set by the modelled hosts and time steps. Format and access: Java source built with Maven (JDK 21), cloned from GitHub or downloaded as release packages with examples and API documentation; free of charge under the GPL named in its source headers. Caveats: models are abstractions of compute, storage and network, without thermal, electrical or physical-facility detail; many forks exist and results depend on the version. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of data-centre resources, energy studies, resilience of cloud services to host failures, and scheduling experiments for a data-centre digital twin. Related records: CloudSim Plus is a re-engineered fork, iFogSim extends it to fog and edge computing, and SimGrid is an alternative distributed-systems simulator.
